_workspace_root: NOT a config key — pass --workspace-root, or run the daemon from inside the workspace. This lets one config file drive several daemons over different workspaces on the same machine.
_: Every key below can also be given as a CLI flag (--poll-interval, --repo, ...), and the CLI wins. Keys prefixed with _ are comments.
_repos: Allowlist of owner/repo; empty means every repo that requests a review. --repo replaces this list rather than extending it.
_operators: GitHub logins allowed to re-open a capped PR with a `alissa-review: re-enter +N` comment (N up to 5). Empty means no ack is ever honoured; the reviewer identity is never an operator. --operator replaces this list rather than extending it.
_reviewer_login: The GitHub login every verdict must be posted under. null auto-detects it from the gh credential at startup. Either way the daemon re-checks the login before every review it submits and refuses to post as anyone else.
_reviewer_token_env: NAME of the environment variable holding the reviewer identity's GitHub token — never the token itself. Set it and every `gh` call runs under that credential explicitly, with the inherited GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN stripped. Leave it null and the daemon inherits whatever the process was given, and warns at startup: on a host that holds more than one GitHub identity, inheritance is how a round's verdict ends up posted under the wrong login.
_state_path: Omit to default to <workspace-root>/.revloop/state.db, which keeps daemons on different workspaces from sharing a spawn ledger.
_on_missing_hub: 'skip' (default) or 'add' to run `alissa code workspace add`. 'add' requires a non-empty repos allowlist.
_reap_grace_seconds: How long a reviewer session must be idle AND quiet (no tmux activity) before the reap sweep kills it, and before a stale round reads it as dead rather than working. Long enough that a just-merged PR's reviewer can finish its in-session close-out, and REJECTED at or above the 90-minute stale-round window (it also gates the stale-round liveness probe, whose respawn branch it would otherwise make unreachable).
_reap_session_cap: Alarm threshold, not a capacity limit: more live reviewer sessions than this after a sweep and the daemon logs page-worthy. A healthy loop runs a couple of concurrent rounds.
_max_concurrent_sessions: SPAWN GATE. At this many live reviewer sessions of this daemon's own grammar (its own review-<repo>-pr<n>-r<k>-<nonce> spawns AND the skill's hand-spawned review-pr-<n>), an owed round waits for a slot instead of spawning, and is retried on later polls. Deferral costs the round nothing: no round number, no attempt, no stale-round respawn, no operator page; the oldest waiter takes the next free slot. Other lanes' sessions in a shared container are invisible to it, exactly as they are to the reaper. Must be <= reap_session_cap (the loader refuses an alarm below the limit, which would page on healthy load). Sized for the container's CPU budget, not for the review backlog: a reviewer session is a full interactive agent.
_checks_wait_seconds: How long a round holds its APPROVE while the judged head's CI rollup is still running (or unreadable) before recording the verdict as a COMMENT instead. PER CONDITION WAITED ON: an unreadable hold that becomes a genuine pending one restarts the clock once, so the worst-case hold is twice this (the daemon reports both numbers) — an approve from the reviewer identity is the operator's merge cue, so it must mean reviewed AND green. A RED rollup never waits: it posts REQUEST_CHANGES leading with the failing check names. 0 means never hold (degrade on the first poll). Skipped/neutral contexts never block.
_checks_spawn_wait_seconds: PRE-SPAWN CI GATE. How long an owed round waits for the head's checks to CONCLUDE before its reviewer is queued at all. The key above gates the verdict the DAEMON posts; this one is the only structural gate on the verdict a reviewer SESSION posts, which is the normal path — a session that has not started cannot approve ahead of its evidence (studio #560: an approve landed 29s before that head's test job failed). PENDING holds the spawn, re-checked every poll_interval; RED and UNKNOWN queue immediately with a directive that forbids the approve and names the failing checks; past the bound the round is queued anyway with a no-approve directive, because a CI system that never reports must delay a review, not cancel it. A held round costs nothing: no round number, no attempt, no ledger spawn row. 0 disables the hold and relies on the directive alone. It ALSO bounds the reviewer session's own in-round wait: the same number goes into every directive as how long a session may wait for a running check before submitting, floored at 5 minutes so a 0 here cannot read as 'do not wait at all'. Deliberately not checks_wait_seconds -- that bounds the daemon holding a finished verdict, while a waiting session is holding one of max_concurrent_sessions worker slots.
_review_task_miss_ttl_polls: NEGATIVE REVIEW-TASK CACHE. How many polls a PR with NO review task is taken on trust before the daemon searches the task corpus for one again. `alissa task list` is the widest read this daemon makes (the actor's whole live corpus), and the PR -> review-task mapping can only remember an answer that EXISTS — so a third-party PR, or one whose task was validated or retitled, missed the cache on every pass and paid that read for the same answer each time: 1,440 whole-corpus reads a day, per unmapped PR, at the default cadence. A completed search that finds nothing is recorded in the ledger and re-checked after this many polls of that PR; a recorded mapping clears it immediately. What is traded is LATENCY, not correctness: a review task created mid-window is picked up at the re-arm rather than the next poll (10 polls = 10 minutes at the default poll_interval). A ledger that cannot record or spend the answer suppresses nothing and the daemon searches every pass, as it did before this existed. FLOOR 1 — there is no value that disables the cache, and 0 is refused at load rather than silently writing rows nothing reads.
_task_list_self_scope: Narrow `alissa task list` to THIS actor's own rows (--self), dropping the sponsor's corpus. OFF by default on evidence, not caution: on the live fleet corpus (2026-08-16) --self removes 4% of the payload, and 3 of the 371 review tasks in it are among the rows it removes — they are owned by another actor. A review task the list cannot see is a round the daemon cannot count, which is a worse trade than 4% of the wire. Turn it on only where EVERY review task is created by this daemon's own reviewer sessions. Ignored (with a startup warning) when the installed alissa CLI does not advertise the flag; the status filter and digest view are adopted automatically wherever the CLI offers them and need no key here.
